It would not be hard to do all your grocery shopping at Trader Joe’s. The chain grocer has great snacks, frozen entrées, and a bakery corner. But some of its best items, especially this time of year, are the frozen appetizers.

“Trader Joe’s is where you stop on the way to a party,” someone once told me, and I can’t help but agree. If you’re in the mood for something itty-bitty and bite-sized, cheesy and oozy, or dippable and poppable, chances are Trader Joe’s has something new (and often unusual) that’s good enough to plan a party around.
I’ve tasted my way through hundreds of TJ’s frozen apps, both as a customer and former employee, and there were more than a few that stood out. Here’s what I always grab.

My grandma had excellent taste, and the same is true of the grandmas I interviewed last year about their go-to frozen apps. One of those grandmas reminded me of the glory that is Trader Joe’s frozen mini samosas. They’re available in vegetarian potato and pea and chicken varieties. I’m pretty partial to the vegetable samosas. Mira, the aforementioned grandmother of six (and counting!), said it best: “No one is mad to see these samosas on the table.”

One of the newer items to hit TJ’s freezer section, these Hane-Style Beef Gyoza have what I call “serious crossover potential.” By that I mean, the uncanny ability to cross over from being a seriously good appetizer to, oops, it’s now my favorite dinner. In truth, I ate all 12 of these crispy, doughy gyoza with a beef and vegetable filling in one sitting.

Do with that information what you will (grab a few more bags). Also included with purchase? A very fun magic trick reveal after cooking (once you flip the pan to reveal the crunchy “skirt” that appears!).

At a party, I make a beeline for the pigs in a blanket. Every party has them, and you can’t go wrong with this version. The Parmesan Pastry Pups from Trader Joe’s are a more deluxe version of regular ol’ crescent rolled cocktail franks, with a flaky, buttery puff pastry exterior that swaddles the juicy little mini hot dogs ever-so-nicely. When I bring them to a potluck, they always get me invited back.

A large slab of spanakopita is amazing. But sometimes the people in your life want to share, which, FINE. In that case, these mini triangular versions of the classic Greek feta and spinach pie make perfect individual servings.

I’m particularly a fan due to how absolutely loaded these spanakopita are. Air-frying them recently had them nearly bursting through those flaky layers with the cheesy filling in all the best ways. Don’t forget plenty of tzatziki for dipping.

Baked Brie is arguably already a very hands-off app, but I love Trader Joe’s version, which comes pre-wrapped in flaky pastry. It’s a failsafe thing to keep in the fridge when you’ve forgotten you’re hosting a book club, but do not want your snack spread to look like it. And it makes a great party dip, too.

Encased in a crackly, buttery pastry, you’ll find a supremely rich wheel of double-cream Brie that’s ready to be taken in more than a few flavor directions. I’m partial to fig or onion jam, but even a drizzle of honey will add a bit of semi-homemade flair to this frozen wonder.

To me, a great appetizer should be able to pull double duty. That’s why I’m such a fan of these palm-sized fried onion halves. Yes, you can share them among friends as is. But you can also plop them on a burger, cut and sprinkle them onto salad, and add them to an assortment of other tempura-style vegetables.

Think of them as a lightly battered, more open-ended version of an Outback Bloomin’ Onion. They’re not too salty, the sweetness of the onion shines through (and isn’t hidden by too much seasoned batter), plus they crisp up like a dream in the air fryer.

These petite little tarts fully made me into a mushroom-lover, and I’m not alone in the club. Jarrett, a contributor at The Kitchn, agrees, saying these buttery, umami bites are melt-in-your-mouth good. I’m not entirely sure how the creators of these tartelettes shrunk down a meal’s worth of flavor into one small bite (in a very Everlasting Gobstopper way), but they very much nailed it with these super-savory, cheesy bites.

Ke$ha might have once sang that the party doesn’t start ‘til she walks in, but I’d argue she was actually talking about cocktail meatballs. Specifically, these frozen turkey meatballs that I always keep on hand. I like that they’re a lighter alternative to traditional beef and pork meatballs, and also are way more versatile for all kinds of flavor combinations.
I’ve yet to find a sauce combo that doesn’t work well with these turkey meatballs: Grape juice and ketchup, hot honey mustard, tomato sauce, and classic BBQ sauce are all great options.

One thing I was not anticipating was the sheer popularity of this humble tart. In truth, I had never tried it in my customer-only days, but I’m so glad other customers made me see the light when I worked at the grocer and spotted how many of these were bought each day.

Much like the aforementioned gyoza, do not be surprised when this tart accidentally becomes your favorite dinner. In under 10 minutes you’ll have a light, flaky tart that hits all the flavor notes: sweetness from the caramelized onions, salty ham, and punch of nutty Swiss Gruyère to round out the buttery crème fraîche.
10. Feta & Caramelized Onion Pastry Bites, $5.49 for 8.5 ounces

If you’re on the lookout for an app that gives off a “oh, this ol’ thing?” sort of feeling, look no further than these fancy (yet unfussy) pastries. These crispy bites pack in a full meal’s worth of flavor in each two-bite experience: a creamy sharpness from the feta, sweetness from the onions, and flaky pastry that really does melt in your mouth. Even when the Trader Joe’s parking lot looks frightful (as it does), you’ll find it worth it just to grab a few boxes.
